uncited: This method generates unique hierarchical spatial keys for octree cells by recursively concatenating binary octant indices to a parent key.
The bit-length of the key corresponds to the depth of the node in the octree.
- Each octant index is represented by a 3-bit binary value.
Let $k_{parent}$ be the key of the parent node and $o$ be the octant index of the child ($0 \le o \le 7$).
- **Key Size:** Keys grow linearly with depth.
For deep octrees, 64-bit integers may overflow.
- **Root Definition:** The root key is explicitly defined as $1$.
- **Time Complexity:** Key generation is $O(1)$ per node if the parent key is known.
- **Memory Complexity:** Keys are stored as integers.
The size of the key is proportional to the depth of the tree.
- **Strengths:** Simple implementation, efficient parent/child navigation, preserves spatial locality for adjacent nodes at the same level.
- **Limitations:** Keys do not directly encode global coordinates, making spatial queries (e.g., "find all nodes in region X") require tree traversal or additional indexing.
This method is based on Morton coding [Morton, 1966], adapted for octree hierarchical structures.
